title: Eight and thirteen samples retain 95 percent of input information in two fully observed passive worm models
abstract: We tested discrete sampling for constant-input estimation in two passive models of partial adult worm electrical maps. With unit leak, independent equal current noise, exact observation of all 180 cells, count coupling k=1 and a one-leak-time window, 8 and 13 equally spaced samples retained at least 95 percent of continuous-record Fisher information for every spatial input. Every single-cell input needed 7 and 11 samples; the median single-cell input needed 3 in both maps. Counts include both endpoints. We applied established Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-design theory to derive an exact fastest-mode sampling certificate and a conservative sample bound. Dense covariance calculations agreed within 7e-16 relative error. Count and binary weights, three coupling levels and three durations gave 36 settings. The model assumes known symmetric dynamics and stationary input before recording. Partial anatomy, assumed conductances, absent measurement noise and lack of linked activity prevent an experimental frame-rate or biological coding claim. Original code, proof, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External connectivity records are excluded.

display.caption: Sampling requirements for two assumed passive adult worm circuit models. Samples include both endpoints and observe all cells. Count weights and a one-leak-time window are used. Solid lines protect every spatial input; dashed lines protect every single-cell input.
